# Audit checks

<!-- Generated by `python -m searchos.audit.gen_docs` from backend/searchos/audit/catalog.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

The audit runs 41 checks over everything the crawler found. Each check belongs to one of 5 categories and has a severity.

## How the score works

For every check that applied to something on the site, take the share of items that failed it (for a site-wide check that is 0 or 1). Weight each check by its severity and average:

    score = 100 x (1 - sum(weight x failing share) / sum(weight))

| Severity | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| critical | 10 |
| high | 5 |
| medium | 2 |
| low | 1 |
| info | 0 |

A check that applies to nothing (for example the article checks on a site with no articles) is left out. Info checks are reported but do not change the score. Each category has its own subscore computed the same way over that category's checks. When nothing can be scored the score is shown as not available instead of 100.

## Indexability and crawling

### `HTTPS_MISSING` - Site is not served over HTTPS

Severity: **critical** (weight 10). Applies to: `site`.

**Why it matters.** Browsers label http sites "Not secure", Google prefers https, and visitors do not trust or buy from insecure sites.

**How to fix it.** Install an SSL certificate (most hosts offer one free) and redirect all http:// addresses to https://.

### `HTTP_5XX` - Page returns a 5xx server error

Severity: **critical** (weight 10). Applies to: `responding_urls`.

**Why it matters.** The server failed to answer. Repeated server errors make search engines crawl the site less and can remove the affected pages from the index.

**How to fix it.** Check the server or application logs for this URL, fix the underlying error, and confirm the page loads. Ask your host if it keeps happening.

### `REDIRECT_LOOP` - Redirect loop

Severity: **critical** (weight 10). Applies to: `fetched_urls`.

**Why it matters.** The URL redirects back to itself through other URLs, so the page can never load. Browsers show an error and search engines give up.

**How to fix it.** Find the redirect rules involved (server config, CMS or plugin) and remove the one that sends visitors back. Test with a private browser window.

### `BLOCKED_IN_SITEMAP` - Sitemap URL is blocked by robots.txt

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `sitemap_urls`.

**Why it matters.** The sitemap invites search engines to a page that robots.txt forbids them to visit. Neither signal can be followed.

**How to fix it.** Remove the URL from the sitemap, or remove the matching Disallow rule if the page should be crawled.

### `BROKEN_INTERNAL_LINK` - Page links to a broken internal URL

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `html_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Broken links frustrate visitors, waste crawl budget and leak link value to nowhere.

**How to fix it.** Open the page, find the listed links, and either correct the address or remove the link. If the target moved, add a 301 redirect.

### `CANONICAL_TO_NON200` - Canonical points to a URL that is not a normal page

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `internal_canonical_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The canonical target redirects, is missing or is an error page. Search engines then ignore the canonical hint or drop the page.

**How to fix it.** Change the canonical to the final, working address of the page (a URL that answers 200 and is not itself redirected).

### `HTTP_4XX` - Page returns a 4xx error

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `responding_urls`.

**Why it matters.** Visitors and search engines hit an error page instead of content. Pages that errored are dropped from search results, and every link pointing to them is wasted.

**How to fix it.** Restore the page, or redirect (301) the old address to the closest replacement. Then update or remove the internal links that point to it.

### `NOINDEX_IN_SITEMAP` - Page is in the sitemap but marked noindex

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `sitemap_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The sitemap asks search engines to index the page while the page itself says not to. The contradiction wastes crawl budget and Search Console reports it as a warning.

**How to fix it.** Decide which signal is right. To keep the page out of search, remove it from the sitemap. To rank it, remove the noindex tag or X-Robots-Tag header.

### `CANONICAL_MISSING` - Canonical tag missing

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Without a canonical tag, search engines have to guess which address of the page is the main one, which can split ranking signals between duplicates (with and without parameters, trailing slashes, and so on).

**How to fix it.** Add <link rel="canonical" href="https://your-site/the-page"> to the head, pointing at the page's own preferred address. Most SEO plugins can do this for every page.

### `MIXED_CONTENT` - Secure page loads insecure (http) resources

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `https_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Browsers block or warn about insecure images, scripts and styles on a secure page, which breaks the page and erodes trust.

**How to fix it.** Change the listed http:// addresses to https://, or host the files on your own secure domain.

### `ORPHAN_PAGE` - Orphan page (in the sitemap, no internal links)

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `sitemap_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Pages nobody links to are hard to discover and receive no link value from the rest of the site.

**How to fix it.** Link to the page from relevant pages and menus, or remove it from the sitemap if it is not needed.

### `REDIRECT_CHAIN` - Redirect chain (more than one hop)

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `fetched_urls`.

**Why it matters.** Each extra redirect slows the page and loses a little of the link value. Search engines may stop following a long chain.

**How to fix it.** Point the first URL straight at the final destination with a single 301, and update internal links to use the final URL.

### `SITEMAP_MISSING` - No XML sitemap found

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `site`.

**Why it matters.** A sitemap tells search engines which pages exist and helps new pages get found faster.

**How to fix it.** Generate a sitemap (most SEO plugins do) and list it in robots.txt with a Sitemap: line.

### `CANONICAL_MISMATCH` - Canonical points to a different page

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `internal_canonical_pages`.

**Why it matters.** This page tells search engines that another page is the main version, so this one is unlikely to rank. That is right for duplicates and wrong when the page should rank on its own.

**How to fix it.** If the page is a real duplicate, nothing to do. If it should rank itself, change the canonical to its own address.

### `DEEP_PAGE` - Page is more than 4 clicks from the homepage

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `html_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Pages buried deep in the site are crawled less often and are seen as less important.

**How to fix it.** Add links from higher-level pages, category pages or the menu so the page is within 3 to 4 clicks.

### `ROBOTS_MISSING` - No robots.txt file

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `site`.

**Why it matters.** Without robots.txt you cannot point crawlers to your sitemap or keep them out of private areas.

**How to fix it.** Create a robots.txt at the root of the site. A minimal one is "User-agent: *" followed by a Sitemap: line.

## On-page content

### `TITLE_MISSING` - Title tag missing

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The title is the clickable headline in search results and the strongest on-page signal. Without it Google makes up a title, usually a poor one.

**How to fix it.** Write a unique title of 30 to 60 characters that names the page's topic, and put it in the <title> tag.

### `H1_MISSING` - Main heading (H1) missing

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The H1 tells readers and search engines what the page is about at a glance.

**How to fix it.** Add one H1 heading near the top of the page that states the topic.

### `HREFLANG_INVALID` - Invalid hreflang annotation

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `hreflang_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Search engines ignore hreflang tags that use wrong language codes or relative links, so visitors may be shown the wrong language version.

**How to fix it.** Use valid codes (en, en-GB, x-default), absolute URLs, and list each code only once per page.

### `META_DESC_MISSING` - Meta description missing

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The meta description is the text under the title in search results. Without it Google picks a random snippet, which usually gets fewer clicks.

**How to fix it.** Write a unique summary of about 120 to 155 characters that tells people why to click, and add it as the page's meta description.

### `THIN_CONTENT` - Thin content (under 250 words)

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Pages with very little text rarely rank for anything and AI assistants have little to quote. This counts the main text of the page without menus and footers, as it appears in the raw HTML.

**How to fix it.** Add useful, original content that answers what visitors came for. If the page is not meant to rank, mark it noindex instead. If the text is added by JavaScript, make it part of the server-rendered HTML.

### `TITLE_DUPLICATE` - Duplicate title

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Pages with identical titles compete with each other and are hard to tell apart in search results.

**How to fix it.** Give every page its own title that describes what is special about that page.

### `VIEWPORT_MISSING` - Mobile viewport tag missing

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Without it phones show a shrunken desktop page. Google indexes the mobile version of a site first.

**How to fix it.** Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the head.

### `H1_MULTIPLE` - More than one H1 heading

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Several H1s blur the page's main topic. HTML allows it, but one clear main heading works best.

**How to fix it.** Keep one H1 and turn the others into H2 or H3 headings.

### `IMG_ALT_MISSING` - Image without alt text

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Alt text describes images to screen readers and to search engines, and helps images appear in image search. (An empty alt="" is fine for purely decorative images.)

**How to fix it.** Add a short, descriptive alt attribute to each meaningful image.

### `LANG_MISSING` - Page language not declared

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The lang attribute helps browsers, screen readers and search engines pick the right language handling.

**How to fix it.** Add a lang attribute to the html tag, for example <html lang="en">.

### `META_DESC_DUPLICATE` - Duplicate meta description

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** The same description on several pages gives searchers no reason to choose one over the other.

**How to fix it.** Write a unique description for each page.

### `TITLE_LENGTH` - Title too short or too long

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Titles over about 60 characters are cut off in search results; very short titles waste the best on-page space for keywords.

**How to fix it.** Rewrite the title to be between 30 and 60 characters, with the main topic first.

## Structured data

### `SCHEMA_PARSE_ERROR` - Structured data (JSON-LD) cannot be parsed

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `html_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Broken JSON-LD is ignored entirely, so the page loses rich results and AI assistants cannot read its facts.

**How to fix it.** Fix the syntax error shown (often a trailing comma or missing quote). Check it with Google's Rich Results Test or schema.org's validator.

### `ORG_SCHEMA_MISSING` - Homepage has no Organization structured data

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `homepage`.

**Why it matters.** Organization markup tells search engines and AI assistants who you are, your logo and official profiles, which helps knowledge panels and correct brand answers.

**How to fix it.** Add Organization (or LocalBusiness) JSON-LD with name, url and logo to the homepage.

### `SCHEMA_REQUIRED_PROP_MISSING` - Structured data missing required properties

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `html_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Incomplete markup is not eligible for rich results and gives AI assistants unreliable facts.

**How to fix it.** Add the missing properties listed (for example name, offers or author) to the JSON-LD for this page.

## Performance

### `CWV_CLS_POOR` - Cumulative Layout Shift is poor (over 0.25)

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `psi_cls_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) measures how much the page jumps around while loading. Over 0.25 is rated "poor" by Google's Core Web Vitals and makes visitors misclick. Taken from real Chrome users (field data) when available, otherwise from a single simulated load (lab).

**How to fix it.** Give images, videos, ads and embeds explicit width and height, reserve space for banners and late-loading content, and avoid inserting content above what is already visible.

### `CWV_INP_POOR` - Interaction to Next Paint is poor (over 500 ms)

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `psi_inp_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Interaction to Next Paint (INP) measures how quickly the page reacts to clicks and taps. Over 500 ms is rated "poor" by Google's Core Web Vitals. It is only available from real-user (field) data, so it is checked only for pages Google has enough visitor data for; it is never estimated from a lab test.

**How to fix it.** Break up long JavaScript tasks, remove or defer heavy third-party scripts (chat widgets, tag managers, trackers), and avoid expensive work in click and input handlers.

### `CWV_LCP_POOR` - Largest Contentful Paint is poor (over 4 seconds)

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `psi_lcp_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is how long the main content takes to appear. Over 4 seconds is rated "poor" by Google's Core Web Vitals, which are a ranking signal and a strong predictor of visitors leaving. Taken from real Chrome users (field data) when Google has enough of them for this page, otherwise from a single simulated load (lab). Only pages with PageSpeed Insights data are checked.

**How to fix it.** Compress and properly size the hero image or main text block, serve it from a CDN, preload it, remove render-blocking scripts and styles above the fold, and speed up the server response.

### `TTFB_SLOW` - Slow server response (over 800 ms)

Severity: **medium** (weight 2). Applies to: `indexable_pages`.

**Why it matters.** A slow first byte delays everything else and hurts Core Web Vitals, rankings and conversions. Measured from our crawler, so it is a guide rather than an exact visitor experience.

**How to fix it.** Turn on page caching or a CDN, upgrade slow hosting, and look for heavy database queries or plugins on this page.

## AI readiness

### `AI_SEARCH_BOT_BLOCKED` - robots.txt blocks AI search or assistant crawlers

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `site`.

**Why it matters.** Bots such as OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot or Claude-SearchBot fetch pages to answer users' questions and cite their sources. If they are blocked, your site cannot be quoted or linked in those answers.

**How to fix it.** Remove the Disallow rule for the listed bots in robots.txt unless blocking them is a deliberate choice.

### `JS_DEPENDENT_CONTENT` - Main content only appears after JavaScript runs

Severity: **high** (weight 5). Applies to: `rendered_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Most AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) do not run JavaScript, so they see an almost empty page. We compare the text in the raw HTML with the text in a real browser; flagged when the raw HTML holds under half of it.

**How to fix it.** Render the content on the server (server-side rendering or static generation) so it is in the first HTML response.

### `ANSWER_BLOCK_MISSING` - Question heading without a short answer (heuristic)

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `question_pages`.

**Why it matters.** AI assistants and featured snippets prefer a direct answer right under a question. This is a heuristic: it looks for question-style H2/H3 headings that are not immediately followed by a paragraph of 80 words or fewer.

**How to fix it.** Put a one to three sentence answer directly under the question, then expand below it.

### `AUTHOR_DATE_MISSING` - Article without a visible author or date

Severity: **low** (weight 1). Applies to: `article_pages`.

**Why it matters.** Authorship and freshness are trust signals for readers, search engines and AI assistants deciding what to cite.

**How to fix it.** Show the author's name and the publish date on the page and add author and datePublished to its Article markup.

### `AI_TRAINING_BOT_BLOCKED` - robots.txt blocks AI training crawlers

Severity: **info** (weight 0). Applies to: `site`.

**Why it matters.** Bots such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot collect content to train AI models. Blocking them is a legitimate choice and does not affect search or AI answers, so this is shown for information only.

**How to fix it.** Nothing to fix if intended. To allow training use, remove the Disallow rule for the listed bots.

### `LLMS_TXT` - No llms.txt file (information only)

Severity: **info** (weight 0). Applies to: `site`.

**Why it matters.** llms.txt is a proposed file that summarises your site for AI tools. No major search or AI engine has confirmed using it, so it is not scored.

**How to fix it.** Optional. If you want one, publish a short markdown file at /llms.txt describing the site and linking to key pages.

## AI crawlers checked in robots.txt

Blocking a search or user-fetch bot is a high-severity issue because the site can then not appear in that assistant's answers. Blocking a training bot is only information: it is a choice.
